what_it_does: Hypergraph neural networks extend ordinary graph neural networks to handle relationships that connect more than two nodes at once — for example, a research paper that links multiple authors and topics simultaneously. Computing with hypergraphs involves two passes: one aggregating information from all nodes in a relationship (a hyperedge), and one aggregating back from hyperedges to nodes. The standard approach runs these passes independently and recomputes intermediate results multiple times, wasting work. MeHyper identifies the fine-grained shared pieces of information (called microedges) that appear in multiple aggregation tasks, computes each shared piece only once, and then distributes it to every task that needs it. A custom accelerator chip implements this microedge-centric computation with a pipelined design and a tiered on-chip memory layout that keeps reused intermediate values close to the math units, reducing expensive trips to large off-chip memory.
